info.title: Nohead API
info.description:
The Nohead API manages projects, collections (your data models), their
fields, and records (your content), with full version history.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Servers, CI and agents use a
project API key (`sk_live_...`, created in the web app under API keys)
with scopes such as `records:read` or `schema:write`. Organization,
project, member and API key management need a person signed in to the
web app and are not available to API keys.

## Resources and IDs

Every object has an opaque, prefixed `id` (`col_`, `fld_`, `rec_`, ...)
and an `object` type. Record values live under `data`, keyed by each
field's `api_key`. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC. Deletes are soft and
can be undone.

## Lists

Lists return `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "next_cursor", "has_more" } }`.
Pass `limit` (1-100) and `cursor` to page, and `sort` (prefix `-` for
descending). Records also take `filter[<api_key>]=value`,
`filter[published_at][exists]=true` and `expand=<relation, asset or
rich text fields>`.

## Errors

Errors share one envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "message",
"request_id", "details" } }`. `details` lists field-level problems as
`{ "field", "code", "message" }`. Include the `request_id` when asking
for support.

## Safe retries and concurrent edits

Send `Idempotency-Key` on any `POST`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` to make retrying
it safe: the first result is stored for 24 hours and returned again for
the same request. Record responses carry the record's revision as an
`ETag`; send it back as `If-Match` to update only if nobody changed the
record in the meantime (`412` otherwise).

## History

Every change to a record is a revision, attributed to the person or API
key that made it: record revisions can be listed, diffed and reverted,
and collections keep a schema history. Send `Nohead-Change-Note` to
record why a change was made. Changes that rewrite existing values
(such as a field's type) are explicit, previewable field migrations.

How long revisions are kept depends on the organization's plan. Older
ones are removed, but every record keeps its first revision and its
last 10; `history_pruned_through` says how far history was removed.

tags.name: records
tags.description: Content entries, one at a time or many at once.

tags.name: publishing
tags.description: Making records live, now or at a set time, and taking them down.

tags.name: revisions
tags.description: A record's history, comparing two revisions, and going back to one.

tags.name: drafts
tags.description: Changes to a record that wait to be merged into it, now or at a set time.

tags.description: A collection's schema history, and its schema at any version.

tags.description: Explicit field changes that rewrite existing record values, with previews.

tags.description: Files stored for a project, uploaded directly to storage.

tags.description: Full-text search in collections and across a project.

tags.description: Event notifications sent to your URLs, and the secrets that sign them.

tags.description: Each event sent to a webhook, its attempts, and retrying it.

tags.description: The append-only trail of who changed what, through which client.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `published_at` (unpublished
records first), or the API key of a text, number, boolean, date or
enum field with one value (records without a value last, in both
directions; text by code point). `-` for descending.

post.description: Creates an unpublished record (revision 1).

get.description:
Also a soft-deleted record, with `deleted_at` and `purge_after` set,
so it can be reviewed and restored. Published-only API keys find
published records only.

patch.description:
Partial update. Keys present in `data` replace their values; `null`
clears one. `409` with detail code `deleted` while the record is
soft-deleted: restore it first.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the record: values and history are kept, and it can be
restored until `purge_after`. Its schedule is cancelled. Deleting a
deleted record changes nothing.

get.description: How many records match the filters, which work as in the list.

post.description:
Publishes, unpublishes, deletes, restores or updates
(`update` with `data`, applied to each) up to 100 records. Each record
is changed as if by its own request: one revision per effective
change, with its own audit event, webhook and search update. Records
that fail (not found, invalid, over a plan limit, a live record with
a pending draft for `publish`) are reported without stopping the
others. Publishing needs `records:publish`; the rest `records:write`.

200.description: What happened to each record, in request order.

post.description:
Brings a soft-deleted record back; restoring one that isn't deleted
changes nothing. `409` when another record took one of its `unique`
values meanwhile (detail code `taken`, with that record's `record_id`).

get.description:
What is live: since when, by whom, and the revision. `404` with detail
code `not_published` while the record is unpublished or deleted.
Published-only API keys get `403`: who published is not content.

post.description:
Makes the record's current content live (`records:publish`), as a
`publish` revision. Publishing a published record changes nothing,
but a live record with a pending draft is `409` with detail code
`draft_pending` and its `draft_id`: publishing never merges a draft
(`POST /v1/drafts/{id}/merge` does). An unpublished record goes live
with its current content and keeps its draft.

delete.description:
Takes the record offline (`records:publish`), as an `unpublish`
revision; its content is kept. Unpublishing an unpublished record
changes nothing.

get.description:
When the record publishes or unpublishes on its own. `404` with detail
code `not_scheduled` when it has no schedule and no `last_error`.
Published-only API keys get `403`.

put.description:
Publishes (`publish_at`) or unpublishes (`unpublish_at`) the record at
a future time (`records:publish`). The change is made within a minute of
the time, like a manual publish from the scheduler: it has its own
revision (`via: scheduler`), webhooks and audit event. `publish_at`
needs an unpublished record; `unpublish_at` needs a published record or a
`publish_at` before it. Setting or cancelling a schedule is audited but
makes no revision. `409` with detail code `deleted` while the record is
soft-deleted.

get.description:
Every pending scheduled change of the collection's records, soonest
first (`sort=-at` for the latest first): publishes and unpublishes
from records' schedules, and merges from drafts' (`draft_id`). One per
change, so a record due to publish and later unpublish appears twice.
Deleted records have none. Published-only API keys get `403`.
The record's history, newest first. Available while the record is soft-deleted.

200.description: The revision with its snapshot and changes.

post.description:
Writes a new `revert` revision whose data is the target revision mapped
onto the current schema. With `dry_run=true`, returns a preview and
writes nothing; the preview shows the old revision's data, so it also
needs `records:read`.

200.description: The reverted record, or a preview for dry runs.
Changes from one revision to another.

get.description:
The record's draft, as a list: a record has at most one for now. Empty
while the record is deleted, whose draft is hidden until it is
restored. Published-only API keys get `403`.

post.description:
Starts the record's draft (`records:write`): changes to its content
that wait until they are merged, now or at a set time, while the
record keeps its current values. `data` takes values as a record
update does, validated on what the record would read after the
merge. With `from_revision`, the draft starts from that revision's
values (mapped onto the current schema, as a revert is), to bring an
earlier version back for review. Works on any record, live or not.

One draft per record: a second is `409` with detail code
`draft_exists` and its `draft_id`, so change that one instead. `409`
with detail code `deleted` while the record is soft-deleted.

get.description:
The drafts of the collection's records, most recently changed first,
for "changes pending" badges: a record's representation is only its
content. `filter[record_id]` takes a record ID, or up to 100 with
`filter[record_id][in]=rec_1,rec_2`. Deleted records' drafts are left
out. Published-only API keys get `403`.

The draft, with `data` as the record would read after the merge, so a
site's preview route can render it; `expand` embeds what its relation
and asset fields point at, as for a record. `404` while the record is
deleted. Published-only API keys get `403`.

patch.description:
Changes the draft's values (`records:write`), as a record update
does: keys present in `data` replace their values, and `null` clears
one. A value set back to the record's drops out of the draft.

delete.description:
Discards the draft for good (`records:write`); the record is
unchanged. Returns the draft as it was. The activity log keeps that
it existed (`draft.discarded`).

post.description:
Applies the draft to its record now (`records:write`), as one `merge`
revision that names the draft and its authors, then removes the
draft; returns the record. Content only: the record stays live or
unpublished as it was, and `published_at` keeps its date. Fields the
record changed since the draft started (`base_revision`) keep their
values, unless the draft changes them too. The result is validated
as a record update is, and unique values are checked again (`422`).
Webhooks get `record.updated` with the `draft_id`.

put.description:
Merges the draft at `merge_at`, a future time (`records:write`),
within a minute of it, from the scheduler (`via: scheduler`). The
merge uses the draft as it is then. One that can't be made leaves the
draft as it is, with `schedule.last_error` (and `draft.schedule_failed`).
Returns the draft. A merge due while the record is deleted waits;
once its time has passed, restoring the record drops it, with
`last_error`.

get.description: The project's collections. With `filter[deleted]=true`, the deleted ones, until they are purged; published-only API keys get `403` for those.

post.description: Creates a collection, optionally with initial fields, as schema version 1.

get.description:
Also a deleted collection, with `deleted_at` and `purge_after`, so it
can be reviewed and restored (published-only API keys: active ones
only). Its fields, records and search are `404` until it is restored.

200.description: The collection with its active fields.

patch.description:
Changing the slug breaks clients that address the collection by slug.
`409` with detail code `deleted` while the collection is deleted.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the collection. Fields, records and history are kept, and
it can be restored until `purge_after`. Deleting a deleted collection
changes nothing.

get.summary: Get the schema at a version
get.description: Published-only API keys read only the current version; earlier ones are `403`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Schema version; defaults to the current one.

200.description: The full schema definition at that version.

get.description: The collection's schema history, newest first. Published-only API keys get `403`.
Published-only API keys get `403`.

200.description: The schema change with before/after definitions.

get.description: The collection's fields, in position order (the record editor's). With `filter[deleted]=true`, its deleted fields, in the order they were created; published-only API keys get `403` for those.

patch.description:
Changes that keep existing record values valid. After an `api_key`
change the old key keeps working for 6 months as an alias (see
`aliases`), so clients have time to move. Changing `type` or `multiple`, or a
`configuration` that existing active records would violate, is rejected
with `requires_migration`: use `POST /v1/fields/{field_id}/migrations`.
`409` with detail code `deleted` while the field is deleted.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the field. Record values are kept and hidden until it is
restored, or purged after `purge_after`. Deleting a deleted field
changes nothing.

get.description: The collection's active fields in order, the order of the record editor and of schema listings.

put.description:
Puts the collection's active fields in the given order as one schema
change. `field_ids` must list every active field exactly once.

delete.summary: Stop accepting a renamed field's old key
delete.description:
Removes an alias before it expires (`schema:write`): clients using the
old key stop working at once. Audited as `field.alias_removed`.

post.description:
Brings a deleted field back with its values. `409` (detail code
`duplicate_values`) for a unique field whose values records share
now.

get.description: The collection's field migrations, newest first. Published-only API keys get `403`.

post.description:
Changes a field in a way that rewrites existing record values: its
`type`, `multiple`, a stricter `configuration`, a date's
`include_time`, or making it `required` with a `backfill` for records
that have no value.

Every record is checked first. With `dry_run=true` the result is a
preview: counts per outcome and sample records, nothing written. Without
it, a migration whose values do not all convert is refused (`422`)
unless `on_invalid` is `clear`; otherwise it is accepted (`202`) and
applied in the background. Poll `GET /v1/migrations/{migration_id}`.

While a migration is pending or running, schema writes to the collection
return `409`, and record writes do once it is running (a pending one may
wait for others to finish). A value written while it waits that does
not convert fails the migration, or is cleared with `on_invalid: clear`. Each record whose data changes gets a
`migrate` revision, so cleared or converted values stay recoverable.
A dry run's preview shows sample record values, so it also needs
`records:read`.

202.description: The migration was accepted and will be applied in the background.

get.description: Published-only API keys get `403`.

post.description:
A pending migration is cancelled at once. A running one stops at its
next batch and is rolled back entirely (`cancel_requested_at` is set
until then). Finished migrations cannot be cancelled (`409`).

get.description:
The project's assets, newest first, filtered by `filter[deleted]` and
`filter[content_type]`. Published-only API keys get `403`: sites reach
assets through records (`expand=`), one at a time.

post.description:
Step 1 of uploading a file. Returns the pending asset with its `upload`:
send the file's bytes with `upload.method` to `upload.url`, with
`upload.headers`, before `upload.expires_at`. The bytes go directly to
storage, not through this API. Then call
`POST /v1/assets/{asset_id}/complete`.

`content_type` and `byte_size` must be the file's; storage refuses another
content type and completion refuses another size.

The file counts toward the organization's storage from here on, while it
uploads too. On plans where storage is a hard limit (Free), a file that
would go over it is refused with `402 plan_limit_exceeded`; on others,
`Nohead-Usage-Warning` reports going over.

A project can have at most 100 uploads in progress (started within the
upload's lifetime, not yet completed or deleted); past that, `409` with
`too_many_uploads`. Uploads never completed are removed after a day.

201.description: The pending asset, with where to upload it.

post.description:
Step 2 of uploading a file: verifies the uploaded file (it exists, with the
declared size and content type), reads image dimensions and marks the asset
`ready`. Only ready assets can be used in records. Safe to retry: a ready
asset is returned unchanged. `422 upload_missing` means the file has not
been uploaded yet; `422 upload_mismatch` means it differed from what was
declared, and the asset is marked `failed`. `409` if the file was uploaded
again while it was being checked: complete it again.

get.description:
Also a deleted asset, with `deleted_at` and `purge_after`, until it is
purged. Published-only API keys find only ready assets that published
records use.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the asset. The original is kept for 30 days, then purged;
records that reference it keep the ID. Until then it can be restored,
and image URLs already handed out keep working. To remove it sooner,
purge it (`POST /v1/assets/{asset_id}/purge`). Deleting a deleted asset
changes nothing.

get.description:
A signed URL for a transformed rendition of a ready image asset
(JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or AVIF). The same asset and options always give
the same URL, so it can be cached and embedded; it does not expire.
Only these options can be requested, so nobody can generate other
transformations. Without options it serves the original size. A width
or height on its own rounds up to the next of 16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128,
160, 192, 256, 320, 384, 480, 512, 640, 768, 800, 960, 1024, 1200, 1280,
1536, 1600, 1920, 2048, 2560, 3072, 3840 and 4096; with both, the larger
does and the other keeps its ratio to it, rounded up to a multiple of
1/32. Quality rounds up to a multiple of 10. The response says what
was signed. `409` for an upload not yet completed, and with detail
code `deleted` for a deleted asset.

parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: `contain` fits inside width × height; `cover` fills it, cropping; `fill` stretches to it.

get.description:
A short-lived URL (2 minutes) that downloads the original file under its
filename: ask for it when the download starts, not ahead of time. A
download that has started finishes however long it takes. `409` for an
upload not yet completed, and with detail code `deleted` for a deleted
asset.

get.summary: See where an asset is used
get.description:
The undeleted records that use the asset, through an asset field or
as an image in a rich text field: how many, how many of them are
published, and the 10 most recently updated with the fields they use
it in. Record history does not count. Needs `records:read` too, as
it shows records; published-only API keys get `403`.

post.description:
Removes a deleted asset's original from storage now, instead of 30
days after the delete, and frees its storage. It cannot be restored.
Records that reference it keep the ID, which no longer resolves. Its
image URLs stop working within a minute or so (the CDN's copies are
cleared), though browsers keep copies they already cached. An asset
that is not deleted is a `409`: delete it first.

200.description: The purged asset, as it was.

get.description:
Full-text search in a collection, ranked by relevance (or `sort`).
With an API key, the collection must be `search_enabled` and the words
match its `searchable` fields only; members in the web app search any
collection, on all its text fields. Filters work as in the records list,
on `published_at` (`exists` only) and on fields marked `filterable`
(not on `deleted` or the other timestamps); `sort` on `created_at`, `updated_at`, `published_at` and
fields marked `sortable` (`-` for descending).
Results are the current records; changes appear within seconds. At
most the first 1,000 hits can be paged through. `expand` embeds related
records and assets as in the records list. `409` when search is not
enabled for API keys, while a new collection's index is first built,
and when filtering or sorting on a field newly made `filterable` or
`sortable` until the rebuild that adds it has run (detail code
`rebuilding`; the index status is `stale` meanwhile).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to search for; empty matches everything.

get.description:
One ranked list of matching records from the project's collections (or
those in `filter[collection]`): with an API key, those with
`search_enabled`, matching their `searchable` fields as in a collection
search. `filter[published_at][exists]` narrows to published records
(`true`) or unpublished ones.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to search for; empty matches everything.

collection.description:
A collection slug or ID (`filter[collection]=posts`), or up
to 100 of them (`filter[collection][in]=posts,pages`).

get.description: Whether the collection's search index is built and up to date.

post.description:
Rebuilds the collection's index from its records in the background.
Search keeps working with the current index until the new one is ready.
Rarely needed: indexes follow record and schema changes automatically.
Limited to a few an hour per collection and per organization (`429`).

get.description: The project's webhooks. With `filter[deleted]=true`, the deleted ones, until they are purged.

post.description:
Subscribes a URL to events. The response includes the endpoint's first
signing `secret`, shown only here; verify deliveries with it (see the
`webhooks` section of this document). Rotate it with
`POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/secrets`.

201.description: The webhook, with its signing secret.

get.description: Also a deleted webhook, with `deleted_at` and `purge_after`, so it can be restored.

patch.description:
Change the URL, description, event types, or turn it off (`enabled: false`).
`409` with detail code `deleted` while the webhook is deleted.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the webhook: it can be restored until `purge_after`, with
its delivery log. Pending deliveries to it fail at their next attempt.
Deleting a deleted webhook changes nothing.

post.description:
Sends a `webhook.test` event to this webhook only. `409` if it is
disabled.

get.description: The secrets that sign its deliveries now, oldest first, without their values.

post.description:
Adds a secret, shown only in this response. Deliveries are signed with
it from now on, and with the secrets before it for 24 hours more
(Standard Webhooks sends several signatures), so receivers can switch
without rejecting any. Retire an old one sooner with
`DELETE /v1/webhook-secrets/{secret_id}`.

201.description: The new secret, with its value.

delete.description:
Stops signing deliveries with it now, instead of 24 hours after a newer
one was added. The newest secret can't be retired (`409` with detail
code `newest_secret`): rotate first. Retiring a retired secret changes
nothing.

post.description:
Brings a deleted webhook back, with its settings and secrets, until
`purge_after`. Deliveries that came due while it was deleted failed;
attempt them again with `POST /v1/webhook-deliveries/{delivery_id}/attempts`.
Restoring counts against the plan's webhook limit (`402`).

get.description: The webhook's deliveries, newest first. Kept for 30 days.
The delivery with its payload and every attempt.

post.description:
Attempts the delivery again now, whatever its status; the attempt runs
in the background, and the delivery's `attempts` show it. `409` with
detail code `deleted` if the webhook was deleted.

get.description:
The project's audit events, newest first. API keys need the `audit:read`
scope and see their own project only.
Returns the service status. Does not require authentication.

The user or API key making the request. API key clients use it to
discover their project and scopes.

Feature flags evaluated for the caller. Without credentials,
only public flags are returned, evaluated without actors (for the
marketing website). With a session or API key, client flags are
included, evaluated for the user and the given organization/project
(API keys: their own project). Server flags are never returned.

post.description:
Sent to each subscribed webhook when something happens in a project.
Delivery is at least once: the same event can arrive more than once, so
process events idempotently, keyed by `webhook-id`. Respond with any
2xx within 10 seconds; other responses and timeouts are retried 7
times over about a day.

Requests follow the Standard Webhooks specification
(https://www.standardwebhooks.com), so its libraries verify them:
`webhook-signature` is `v1,` followed by the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of
`{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`, keyed with the base64-decoded
part of the webhook's `whsec_` secret. For a day after the secret is
rotated, the header holds a signature for each signing secret,
space-separated: accept the request when any of them verifies. Reject
requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes away from your clock.

apiKey.description:
Project-scoped API key, e.g. `sk_live_k7fz0a9c3m2q_<secret>`. Used by
servers, CI, the CLI and coding agents.

session.name: __Host-nohead_session
session.description:
A person signed in to the web app: the httpOnly cookie its sign-in
sets, accepted only on requests from the web app's origin (named
`nohead_session` over plain http, in local development). Servers,
CI, the CLI and agents use an API key.

CollectionRef.name: collection_id
CollectionRef.description: Collection ID, or the collection slug when authenticating with an API key.

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description: Comma-separated relation, asset or rich text field API keys whose records or assets to embed under `expanded` (at most 5); for a rich text field, the assets its images show. Embedding needs permission to read what is embedded: `records:read` for relations, `assets:read` for assets and rich text (`403` otherwise).

RecordFilter.name: filter
RecordFilter.description:
`filter[<key>]=value` (equal), or `filter[<key>][<operator>]=value`;
filters combine with AND. Keys are field API keys, `published_at`,
`deleted` (`true` lists soft-deleted records instead) and, in record
lists and counts, `created_at` and `updated_at`. In search,
`published_at` takes only `exists`.

- `eq`, `ne`: equal, not equal. For fields with several values,
  "contains" and "does not contain". `ne` matches records with no value.
- `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`: integer, decimal and date fields with one
  value, and the timestamps.
- `in`: any of up to 100 comma-separated values (`\,` is a comma
  inside a value, `\\` a backslash); for fields with several values,
  "contains any of".
- `exists`: `true` for records with a value, `false` for those without
  (and `published_at`: published or not).

Values are parsed per field type (`"5"` is not the integer 5), but
not held to the field's limits or format (`price[lt]=10` works when
`max` is 5; a slug filter that isn't a slug matches nothing). Dates
take `today`, and dates with a time `now` too. A day (`YYYY-MM-DD`)
given for a date with a time, or a timestamp, covers that day in the
field's `time_zone` (UTC without one): `gte` from its start, `lte` to
its end, `eq` within it. A date with a time matches the same moment
written with any offset.

cheap.summary: Published products under 50 in two categories

AuditEventFilter.name: filter
AuditEventFilter.description:
`action` matches exactly, or by prefix with a trailing `.*`
(`filter[action]=record.*`). `since` is inclusive and `until` exclusive.

DeletedFilter.name: filter
DeletedFilter.description: `filter[deleted]=true` lists soft-deleted items instead of active ones.

AssetFilter.name: filter
AssetFilter.description:
`filter[deleted]=true` lists deleted assets instead.
`filter[content_type]` lists only assets of those types: comma-separated
MIME types or `type/*` wildcards, for example the ones an asset field
accepts (its `accepted_types`).

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The revision you last read (the record's, or the draft's for a draft), e.g. `"7"`. Stale writes fail with 412.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
A unique value (1-255 printable ASCII characters) that makes retrying
this request safe. The first response (below 500) is stored for 24
hours per user or API key; retries with the same key and the same
request get it again with an `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header. The
same key with a different request is refused with `400`; a retry while
the first request is still running gets `409`.

NoheadClient.name: Nohead-Client
NoheadClient.description: First-party client identifier recorded in history (e.g. `cli/0.3.1`). Informational only.

ChangeNote.name: Nohead-Change-Note
ChangeNote.description:
Optional reason for the change, shown in history (at most 500
characters once decoded). Percent-encoded UTF-8, as
`encodeURIComponent` encodes it, so any language fits in a header:
`Rettet%20stavefejl%20p%C3%A5%20forsiden`. Plain ASCII may be sent
as is. Other bytes are `400`.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window. Sent on every authenticated response.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RequestId.description: Unique identifier for the request, also echoed in error bodies.

ETag.description: The current revision (the record's, or the draft's), e.g. `"7"`. Send it back as `If-Match`.

UsageWarning.description:
Set when the organization is over a soft plan limit, as
`<metric>=<usage>/<limit>` (e.g. `api_requests=100234/100000`). Requests
still succeed. Any API-key request may carry it for `api_requests`.

ListMeta.description: Cursor pagination metadata returned with every list.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

RecordFilterValue.description: A value to equal, or operators with their values (see the `filter` parameter).

in.description: Comma-separated; `\,` is a comma inside a value.

id.description: Stable field ID. Never changes, even when the field is renamed.

api_key.description: Key used in record data. Part of the API contract.

required.description: Every record must have a value. Not available for boolean fields (a boolean is true or false; no value reads as false).

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`, an empty string with `blank_value`). Not available for boolean, long_text, rich_text and json fields.

position.description: Where the field sorts in the collection's order, lowest first. New fields are added last; `PUT /v1/collections/{collection_id}/field-order` changes the order, numbering the fields from 0.

configuration.description:
Type-specific options, e.g. `max_length`, `options`, `target_collection_id`,
`accepted_types` (asset fields: MIME types or `type/*` wildcards that newly
written values must have; any file when absent), `include_time` and
`time_zone` (date fields, below), `format` (text fields, below),
`unique` (text and integer fields, below), plus
the options for searches with API keys: `searchable` (the search words match the
field; default true for text, long_text, rich_text and enum), `filterable` and
`sortable` (default false).

Date fields hold a calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, with no time and no
time zone: returned exactly as written, so it never shows as the day
before or after. With `include_time: true` they hold a moment: ISO
8601 with an offset, stored in UTC and returned in UTC, or with the
offset of `time_zone` (an IANA name such as `Europe/Copenhagen`,
daylight saving included) when the field has one. Input may use any
offset. Changing `time_zone` never rewrites values; turning
`include_time` on or off does, through a field migration.

Text fields (not long text) can have a `format`: `slug`
(lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 200
characters; one value per record, never a list, and always
unique: a slug field has `unique: true`), `url` (an absolute
`http` or `https` address) or `email`. A value that doesn't match is
refused with `invalid_format`. A format sets its own length limits
(254 characters for emails, 2,048 for URLs), so `min_length` and
`max_length` are for plain text. Text and integer
fields with one value can be `unique`: no two active records of the
collection share a value (emails compare ignoring capitals; records
without a value don't count). A taken value is refused with
`taken` and the `record_id` that has it. Turning `unique` on is
refused with `duplicate_values` while records share a value (and
so is restoring a deleted unique field, `409`). A field migration
to a unique field is refused with `duplicate_values` when its
converted values or backfill would be shared, and fails if values
written while it waits would be.

deleted_at.description: When the field was deleted; null unless it is. Its values stay hidden in records until it is restored or purged.

purge_after.description: When a deleted field and its values are removed for good, unless restored first.

aliases.description:
Old API keys of a renamed field that still work until `expires_at`:
record data also carries the value under them, and writes, filters,
sorts and `expand` accept them. Responses about the collection then
have `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers.

required.description: Every record must have a value. Not available for boolean fields (a boolean is true or false; no value reads as false).

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`, an empty string with `blank_value`). Not available for boolean, long_text, rich_text and json fields.

required.description: Every record must have a value. Not available for boolean fields (a boolean is true or false; no value reads as false).

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`, an empty string with `blank_value`). Not available for boolean, long_text, rich_text and json fields.

deleted_at.description: When the collection was deleted; null unless it is.

purge_after.description: When a deleted collection is removed for good, with its fields and records, unless restored first.

search_enabled.description:
Whether API keys can search the collection (`GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}/search`).
Every collection is indexed; members can search it in the web app either way.

SchemaDefinition.description: The complete collection definition at one schema version.

id.description: The user (`usr_...`) or API key (`key_...`), or null for system changes.

name.description:
Resolved when read, never stored: a user's current name (or
email), "Deleted user" once they deleted their account, an API
key's name, or "System".

payload.description: Operation details, e.g. `changes` and `breaking` for updates.

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`, an empty string with `blank_value`). Not available for boolean, long_text, rich_text and json fields.

FieldMigrationRequest.description: The parts of the definition to change; omitted parts stay as they are.

configuration.description: The complete new configuration. When the type changes and this is omitted, only `description`, `searchable`, `filterable` and `sortable` carry over.

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`, an empty string with `blank_value`). Not available for boolean, long_text, rich_text and json fields.

backfill.description: Value for active records that have no value, validated like a record value of the new definition; an empty string is refused with `blank_value`.

on_invalid.description: `clear` removes values that cannot be converted (or backfills them); `fail` refuses the migration.

time_zone.description:
When a date field's `include_time` is turned off: the IANA time zone
(e.g. `Europe/Copenhagen`) whose day each moment falls on. Default:
the field's `time_zone`, else UTC. Refused for any other change.

FieldMigrationCounts.description: Records by outcome, including soft-deleted records (which are converted but never backfilled).

conversion.description: `safe`: every value converts unchanged in meaning. `convertible`: every value converts, the representation changes. `conditional`: some values may not convert.

samples.description: Up to 10 affected records, invalid ones first.

before.description: The stored value before the migration, or null.

after.description: The value after the migration, or null when cleared or invalid.

backfill.description: `{"value": ...}` when missing values are filled in, otherwise null.

time_zone.description: The time zone dates were read in when `include_time` was turned off, if one was given.

failure.description: Why the migration failed; null otherwise. A failed migration changed nothing.

cancel_requested_at.description: When cancelling was asked for, while a running migration rolls back.

RecordSchedule.description:
When the record publishes or unpublishes on its own (within a minute of
the time), set with `PUT /v1/records/{record_id}/schedule`. A time is
cleared once it has run. `last_error` explains the last scheduled change
that could not be made, until a new schedule is set.

RecordScheduleUpdate.description: A time in the future, or null for none. Omitted keys keep their value.

published_by.description: Who published it last; null when that revision is no longer kept.

action.description: `publish` and `unpublish` are the record's schedule; `merge` is a draft's.

last_error.description: Why the last scheduled change could not be made, as in the record's (or the draft's) schedule.

Via.description: The client a change came through; `scheduler` for scheduled changes.

Draft.description:
Changes to a record's content that wait until they are merged into
it, now or at `schedule.merge_at`. Content only: whether the record
is live is its publication and schedule.

base_revision.description:
The record's revision when the draft started. Fields the record
changed since keep their values at the merge, unless the draft
changes them too; compare with `GET /v1/records/{id}/diff?from=<base_revision>`.

revision.description: The draft's own revision, 1 when started and one more per change; also returned as the ETag.

data.description: The record's values as they read after the merge.

changed_fields.description: API keys of the fields the draft changes.

edited_by.description: Everyone who changed it since, in order.

expanded.description: Only with `expand`, as on a record, for the values after the merge.

DraftSchedule.description:
When the draft merges on its own (within a minute of the time), set
with `PUT /v1/drafts/{draft_id}/schedule`. `last_error` explains the
last scheduled merge that could not be made, until a new one is set.

from_revision.description: Start from this revision's values instead of the record's current ones.

MergedDraft.description: The draft a `merge` revision merged, which is gone since.

RecordData.description:
Field values keyed by field `api_key`. A rich text value is a
ProseMirror/Tiptap JSON document (`{"type": "doc", "content": [...]}`).
An image of an asset in it is `{"type": "image", "attrs": {"asset_id":
"ast_...", "alt": "..."}}`, between the document's blocks (not inside
a list or quote), at most 100 per document (`too_many_images`); a
newly shown image must be an uploaded JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or AVIF of
the project (`invalid_reference`, `type_not_accepted`). `expand` embeds the assets, and published-only
keys can read the images of published records.

published_at.description: When the record was published; null while it is unpublished.

revision.description: Current revision number; also returned as the ETag.

history_pruned_through.description: Revisions up to this number (except revision 1) were removed by the plan's history retention.

deleted_at.description: When the record was soft-deleted; null unless it is.

purge_after.description: When a soft-deleted record is removed for good, unless restored first.

expanded.description:
Only with `expand`: what each requested relation, asset or rich
text field points at, keyed by field API key: records for
relation fields, assets for asset fields. A single value is the object, or null when
it no longer exists; a multiple value is a list of those that still
exist. For a rich text field, the list of assets its images show,
in document order, leaving out those that no longer exist.
Expanded records are not expanded further.

Change.description:
One change between two states. Field changes carry `field` (current API
key) and the stable `field_id`; attribute changes (`published_at`,
`deleted_at`) carry `attribute`.

changed_fields.description: API keys of changed fields, and changed attributes.

redacted_fields.description:
API keys of fields whose values in this revision were redacted (owners
and admins redact them in the web app); those values read
`{"$redacted": true}`.

draft.description: For a `merge`, the draft it merged, with who started and edited it; null otherwise.

flags.description: Flag name to enabled, for every registered flag the caller may see.

enabled.description: The collection's `search_enabled`; the index is kept up to date either way.

status.description: `building` until first built; `stale` from the change that queues a rebuild until it has run; `failed` if the last rebuild failed (it is retried).

WebhookEventType.description:
An event webhooks can subscribe to: the same names as the activity
log's actions. A subscription can also be every type of a resource
(`record.*`, `draft.*`, `collection.*`, `field.*`, `asset.*`) or `*` for all.

event_types.description: The subscribed event types and wildcards (`record.*`, or `*` for all).

deleted_at.description: When the webhook was deleted; null unless it is.

purge_after.description: When a deleted webhook is removed for good, with its delivery log, unless restored first.

secret.description: The signing secret (`whsec_...`). Keep it private.

expires_at.description: When it stops signing deliveries; null for the newest secret.

secret.description: The signing secret (`whsec_...`), shown only when it is added. Keep it private.

data.description: For `update`, the fields to set on every record (null clears one).

changed.description: False when the record was already in that state (no revision).

project.description: The project the event belongs to, or null for organization-level events.

id.description: The resource's public ID (or key, for feature flags).

via.description: The client the change came through, when known.

metadata.description:
Small, action-specific references, e.g. `revision_id` and
`collection_id` for record events, `schema_change_id` for schema
events, `changed` attribute names for updates. Never content.

url.description: An https URL on the public internet.

id.description: The event ID, sent as `webhook-id`; the same on every attempt.

status.description: `pending` until an attempt gets a 2xx response; `failed` after 8 attempts over about a day.

response_body.description: The first 2 KB of the response.

WebhookEventPayload.description:
The JSON body of every webhook request. It is rendered from the event's
history each time it is sent or shown, so redacted values are redacted
in it too.

id.description: The event's ID, also sent as `webhook-id`; dedupe by it.

type.description: One of the event types (`WebhookEventType`), or `webhook.test`.

actor.description: Who made the change. Always sent.

via.description:
The client the change came through (null when not known). Always
sent. An integration that writes back can skip changes made with
its own API key (`actor`).

data.description:
`record.*`: `record` (as the change's revision left it, or as it is
now for events without a revision such as `record.scheduled`; null
once it is purged), `revision` and `revision_id`; a merged draft's
`record.updated` adds its `draft_id`. `draft.*`: `draft` (as it is
now; null once merged or discarded, and while its record is
deleted), `draft_id` and `record_id`. `asset.*`:
`asset` (as it is now). `collection.*` and `field.*`: `collection`
and `schema_change`, except `field.alias_removed`: `field`.
`webhook.test`: `webhook`.

status.description: `pending` until the upload is completed; only `ready` assets can be used in records.

deleted_at.description: When the asset was deleted; null unless it is.

purge_after.description: When a deleted asset and its file are removed for good, unless restored or purged first.

preview_url.description: A signed URL of a small rendition (fits in 640×640, WebP), for ready images, deleted ones included until they are purged; null otherwise.

records.description: Undeleted records that use the asset.

published.description: Of those, the published ones (what sites show).

uses.description: The most recently updated records that use the asset.

fields.description: API keys of the record's fields that use the asset.

byte_size.description: Exact size of the file in bytes (at most 100 MB by default).

field_ids.description: The collection's active fields, first to last.

AssetWithUpload.description: A new asset with where to upload its file, returned only when it is created.

headers.description: Headers to send with the upload.

ApiKeyScope.description: What a project API key may do. `webhooks:read` includes delivery payloads and `webhooks:write` can subscribe an endpoint to every event, so both give access to the record, schema and asset data in events, unpublished records included; published-only keys cannot have them.

PublishedOnly.description: The key sees published records only, for sites and apps: lists, reads, search and expanded relations leave out unpublished and deleted records, and history is not available. Only read scopes (records:read, schema:read, assets:read, search:read) are allowed.

field.description: API key of the offending field or parameter, when applicable.

current_revision.description: The resource's current revision, for `revision_mismatch` details.

record_id.description: The record that already has the value, for `taken` details.

draft_id.description: The record's draft, for `draft_exists` and `draft_pending` details.

FieldOrder.description: The collection's active fields, in order.

PlanLimitExceeded.description:
The change would exceed a hard limit of the organization's plan. The
detail names the metric (`field`) with its `usage` and `limit`.

Forbidden.description: The caller is not allowed to perform this action.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with current state.

PreconditionFailed.description:
The resource changed since the revision given in `If-Match`. Nothing was
written; `details` includes the current revision.

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests for this API key or user (or, with failing
credentials, this IP address). A published-only key is counted per
client IP. Wait `Retry-After` seconds; retries with the same `Idempotency-Key`
are safe.
